chapter: Brass bands, funerals and working conditions
title: Brass band versus string band: Tuxedo, Olympia, Imperial
summary: Bands such as the Tuxedo (Celestin) had a brass band and a string band. Players doubled, the tuba on string bass, and strings meant banjo and guitar.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: You've spoken of the, uh, some of the bigger bands having, uh, a parade band and string band. Now, uh, how do they, how are they different in composition? Well, like, like the tuxedo, they had a brass band and string band, see.

That, uh, tuxedo, uh, band, was that the Celestan band? Yeah, it was Celestan, yeah. Who were the, did the personnel change any between the string band and the, uh, marching band, or did they just change instruments?

No, they, they add on to the marching band. It's like the, kind of time, the bass, the tuba player would double on string bass. And they'd use the Sam, uh, Celestan always had another trumpet with him. He used two trumpets. Sam trombone.
Did they, uh, ever have any instruments, did they ever have any other string instruments beside the bass, like violin?
No, they had banjo most of the time and guitar.
